NAFDAC Med Safety App
The Med Safety app is a free smartphone app for reporting suspected adverse effects.
The app lets users
Report adverse effects to medicines.
Keep track of previously reported information.
Receive official news and alerts about medicines.
Download it from the Google Play store on Android or the App Store on iOS.

Completing the NAFDAC e-reporting link (for health workers only)
Objective: strengthen pharmacovigilance by making it easy to report suspected ADRs during the AZM MDA.
State teams ensure all OICs, DSNOs and CDD supervisors have access to the link.
They support health facility OICs to upload all suspected ADR cases to the NAFDAC portal.
Click the link to open the page and start.
Vomiting after AZM — record it and report a suspected ADR.
User of the medicine
Initials: instead of the child's initials, write the State code.
State codes: Kaduna-KD, Kebbi-KB, Jigawa-JG, Adamawa-AD, and Gombe-GOM and SARMAAN II. Example: KB(SARMAAN II).
Sex: Male, Female, or Unknown if you are not sure.
Weight: the weight of the child in kg.
Date of birth (compulsory): date, month and year.
User of the medicine, continued
Age at time of reaction: enter the age, then choose year, months, week, day or hours.
For SARMAAN II, the child must be between 1-59 months.
Country where the reaction started: select Nigeria.
Description (click NEXT to continue)
Name of the health facility, LGA and State, e.g. From Musa PHC in Soba LGA, Kaduna State.
Reactions/symptoms, such as vomiting, rashes, fever or diarrhoea.
Start date and end date of the reaction (date, month and year).
Duration: enter a number, then choose year, month, days, weeks or hours.
Outcome (recovered, recovering, recovered with lasting effects, or fatal) and Serious: YES or NO.
Medicines (click NEXT to continue)
Medicine name, e.g. Azithromycin. Tick Probably causing the reaction if you believe the AZM MDA caused it.
Medicine producer: the company name on the AZM bottle. Batch number: from the bottle.
Dosage: the dose given, e.g. 2ml. How administered: select Oral.
Start date: the day the medicine was given. End date: the same day, because it is given once.
Duration: select one Day.
Reason and additional information
Reason for taking the medicine: AZM MDA for prevention of Pneumonia, Diarrhoea and Malaria in the SARMAAN II Project.
Actions taken: select Not applicable.
Additional information: describe any current or previous illness of the child.
Contact details and submit
Profession: select the role.
Given name and family name of the reporting officer.
Health facility name.
Email and phone number of the reporting officer.
Click Submit and wait for the notification that confirms it was submitted.

Role of DSNOs in ADR reporting
Serve as focal persons for referral to health facilities.
Work with CDD supervisors and teams to identify and refer sick children to the nearest facility.
Follow up so all referred cases get care at the nearest supported facility.
Check with OICs that referred children reported and received appropriate care.
Document referral data in the approved reporting template.
Reporting to NAFDAC
Ensure OICs promptly report all confirmed ADRs on the NAFDAC platforms (Med Safety app or e-reporting link).
Collect completed pharmacovigilance forms from health facilities and submit them to NAFDAC.
Tracking referred cases
The State DSNO works with LGA DSNOs to get feedback and solve referral problems.
LGA DSNOs join evening review meetings to update on referrals, challenges and support needed.
LGA DSNOs work with CDD supervisors to find and follow up referred cases until upload on the NAFDAC platform.
LGA DSNOs get OIC feedback for upward referral, recovery status and NAFDAC upload.
Work with the LGA team and community leaders on caregivers' reluctance and knowledge barriers.
Submit the referral template to the State M&E, copying the DPHC and NTD coordinator.
